paper.title: A Relational Tucker Decomposition for Multi-Relational Link Prediction

summarization.summary: This paper proposes Relational Tucker Decomposition (RT) for multi-relational link prediction, generalizing bilinear models by decoupling entity and relation embedding sizes. The authors introduce Sparse RT (SRT), which learns sparsity patterns via $l_0$ regularization rather than relying on fixed constraints. Experiments on FB15K-237 and WN18RR indicate that performance is highly dataset-dependent; while SRT matched or exceeded ComplEx on FB15K-237 with data-driven sparsity, it underperformed relative to ComplEx on the simpler WN18RR dataset. A critical limitation is the significantly higher computational cost of RT training compared to ComplEx (approximately six times longer). Furthermore, no single model consistently dominates across all conditions, and the optimal approach varies based on entity embedding size and relation complexity. The study confirms that hard-coded sparsity is not universally necessary but remains beneficial for specific data characteristics, highlighting the absence of a universally superior method in knowledge graph completion tasks.
